Well, we thought along those lines: First of all, the people that were prone to these [sic] radical moves, that they were the first to join the fighting. Now, whether they were those or not, it was our understanding that they were. "Q. So let me get this straight. Well, I'll put the question another way. Apart from the fact that they -- the simple fact that they went to Croatia to fight, do you know anything else about these [sic] work colleagues of yours which indicated that they were what you regarded as Chetniks? "A. I don't, no." Now, sir, having been refreshed with this testimony from Krajisnik, is it your testimony that these individuals volunteered or chose to go to war or were they mobilised and responding to a legal obligation once mobilised.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I asked the manager because the number of personnel was reduced in my shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I must insist --

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I asked, Where are these people?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're talking about these three individuals, and I'd like to know with respect to these three individuals what exactly is your testimony. Were they mobilised and responding to legal obligations, or did they volunteer and choose to go to fight?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Ivetic. Where in the excerpt that you just read to the witness is anything that could remind him of whether there was mobilisation or volunteering?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In this section, no, Your Honour, but the testimony that he just gave in open court previously was that they responded to call-ups. In his prior testimony he said that they were the first to want to join the fighting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You quoted this to the witness and you said at the end of it, Now that I have read you this and you have refreshed your memory, can you answer me were these people mobilised or did they volunteer. And I'm saying what is it here, from what you quoted to the witness, that reminds witness on whether there was a mobilisation or volunteers?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, my point is to figure out from the witness, since I have two sets of sworn testimony that, to me, appear to be different, to find out what that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I'm suggesting to you quote to the witness a piece of his prior testimony which would remind him about whether these three were mobilised or whether they volunteered. This what you quoted to him doesn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Agreed. Agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So can you do what would remind him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, having heard your testimony from Krajisnik, does it remind you of what you testified in the Krajisnik trial under oath?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I'm trying to answer you, and you stopped me. The manager told me when I said, There are fewer people now. And he said, They were mobilised. Including these three.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we could take the break now. I'm finished with that section and will be moving on to the next section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you indicate us how much time more time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could the witness already be escorted out of the courtroom. Mr. Crncalo, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One hour and 10 minutes, I think, Your Honours. Just outside of that. I will try to finish in less time, but one hour and ten should be the outside limit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if there's not much in re-examination, that would just leave half an hour. And I suggest, Mr. Ivetic, if you say one hour and 10 minutes that you try to squeeze it into the one hour, and if it would be 65 minutes, I think Mr. Mladic would understand. We take a break and return at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, Mr. Ivetic, could you inform me whether you have verified what was said by Mr. Seselj or whether there is any documentary evidence on that. Mr. Lukic, of course, if you want to answer the question, that's fine. But Mr. Ivetic examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I spent the entire break with my client in his cell. I had no opportunity to verify anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I was -- as a matter of fact, you asked the questions in cross-examination, so I was referring rather to what happened before you came into court today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because you're asking questions, you're suggesting that it is an overreaction on certain matters, whereas I would then be interested - and I thought you would be interested to know as well - what Mr. Seselj said at that moment because that might be very important. I think that Mr. Mladic wants to consult with you. He has had an opportunity to do that during the break as we said before. And if Mr. Mladic wants to bring anything to your attention he may now write a little note. And if it's so urgent, Mr. Ivetic, that you think it couldn't wait until the next break, then we'll hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Your Honours, if I may respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In preparations for this witness, I have to go upon what's been disclosed for this witness, what other material we can find. My preparations include reviewing transcripts from everything single proceeding where this witness has testified to, and the corpus of the knowledge and the testimony that he has contained in here, the questions he's been asked by other counsel on these same topics, the answers he's given. And so that was my -- that was where all my questioning comes from, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that you didn't go beyond that and -- because you asked questions about that event, and you apparently were aware of the character of the location where the meeting was held. I don't know whether that -- and the Chamber, of course, is not in a position to verify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The questioning was rather suggestive as that there would be no reason, and we just wondered whether you were also interested in hearing what Mr. Seselj said at that occasion which might support the evidence of the witness or might contradict the evidence of the witness. Mr. Crncalo, Mr. Ivetic will now continue his cross-examination. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to move onto several other matters. First of all, are you aware of the fact that during the years 1991 and 1992, the Bosnian Muslim SDA political party was clandestinely procuring weapons and distributing them to its people in the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I lived in the municipality of Pale. In 1992, it wasn't possible to enter the territory of Pale. It wasn't possible for foreign individuals to enter the territory of Pale. What you're asking me about is something I know nothing of. I am not aware of anyone having obtained weapons in secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Am I correct, sir, that you describe yourself as a sympathizer of the SDA party, albeit it not a member?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record, can you tell us, if you know, about the attack carried out on Renovica village in Pale municipality wherein two Serb policemen were killed and five other Serb policemen were wounded while trying to disarm that village? And, for the record, that was in -- 20 -- 22nd -- well, in May of 1992 [realtime transcript read in error "1991"], sir.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I know about the incident, and that evening after the attack, Malko Koroman, the chief of police, stated on TV, he was in tears, that unfortunately there was war in the municipality of Pale, and he said that two of his policemen had been killed in Renovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay, sir. And do you also have knowledge that - and also in May of 1992 - the Serb civilians of Renovica were expelled from that village by armed Muslim fighters, and, thus, streamed into Pale as refugees?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: When the attack was carried out, as you say, they wanted to confiscate weapons. It was a classic attack on the municipality of -- on the local commune of Renovica because 90 per cent of the population is Muslim down there. Yes, there were some Serbs in Renovica, but they could have withdrawn quite easily with the Serbian forces that were in Renovica, and they could have gone to Pale. I didn't live in Renovica and I couldn't go there, so I'm not in a position to describe things in detail for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir. For the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, just at transcript page 54, line 13, I'd ask Mr. Ivetic to check that line and see if the year he said is correctly recorded there. I believe he said 1992 and the transcript reflects 1991. That's temporary transcript page 54 of today's transcript, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It should be 1992. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record sir, are you aware of the existence of armed Bosnian Muslim fighters in the municipality of Pale in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: There were no fighters, no Muslim fighters in the municipality of Pale. There were the local inhabitants who, well, let's say had lived there for centuries, their parents, their ancestors, their relatives, but as for organised military formations, no, there were no such formations there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us for the record who are Nisad Crncalo and Emir Crncalo and if they have any relation to you?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes, they are relatives of mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were these two individuals either members or sympathizers of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I never tried to verify whether an individual was a member or not. All I can say is that I knew where I stood.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With -- with regard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic. Written notes, nothing else. Otherwise, you will be removed from this courtroom. Last warning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With regard to these individuals I believe you testified in the Krajisnik case they were your cousins. These relatives, in any event, Nisad and Emir Crncalo. You were presented in Krajisnik with the proposition that these individuals had been arrested because they had been trading in illegal weapons. Do you recall that testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the event. They were never involved in a trafficking scheme for food or weapons. They were arrested in the street and I saw that myself. And it's not only they who were arrested, quite a few young people were arrested at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you personally intervened to get them released from custody; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes. It wasn't just me. There were about ten of us who went to see Malko Koroman to ask him about what was happening and why these young people had been arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And eventually, through your efforts, these relatives of yours were released; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Not just these two relatives of mine whose names I have mentioned. There were certainly at least ten young people, young men, who had been arrested on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I put to you, sir, that in Pale municipality, specifically in Praca, that the Bosnian Muslim population there had access not only to hunting and sport guns but also to automatic rifles up to the start of the war in April. Would you agree with that proposition, sir?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I wouldn't. In Renovica there was a military barracks and they were able to control the population. If any military weapons arrived that weren't intended for those barracks, in such cases, disciplinary measures would have been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, your answer specifies Renovica. I'm asking you now go Praca. Are you familiar with Praca?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Of course, I -- of course, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the Muslim males in Praca possessed not only hunting and short guns but also had access to automatic weapons, automatic rifles, up to the start of the war in April?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I'm quite sure that they did not have any such weapons. I could stake my life on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to present to you your sworn testimony in the Karadzic proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 1D288, page 26 in e-court at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Wherein you testified pertaining to questions posed to you by Mr. Karadzic. And when that comes up, it starts at the bottom of the page and goes onto the next page. I will read for you, sir. Please listen carefully. Starting at line 19: "Q. Now, could I draw your attention to the document on the screen dated 28th April. It says: 'As a result of a successful operation by the employees of the public security station in Pale, most Muslims from Praca handed over their weapons today. Automatic rifles, which had been distributed with the mediation of the Praca Imam Fazlo Gljiva were handed over to the authorities. These weapons had arrived in Praca through channels used by Senaid Memic from Hrasnica. This well known Muslim extremist armed members of the Muslim community throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina and from that shipment, 20 automatic rifles arrived in the Praca region.' "Can you see this document? "A. Yes, but these weapons were legally distributed at the police station of Pale to reserve policemen, and those who couldn't muster the courage to bring this rifle and uniform to the police station were returned otherwise. I personally took two rifles from two reserve policemen and turned them over at the police station. "Q. You're talking about weapons that people are issued with when they go on an exercise, be they reserve policemen or reserve soldiers, they get gas masks and uniforms and weapons and they take it all home. "A. That's the way it used to work." Let me stop right there for now. Do you recall this testimony from the Karadzic proceedings, sir.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But you have to allow me to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, how do you reconcile this testimony that you personally surrendered two rifles with your testimony today at line 17 and 18 of page 57 where you said: "I'm quite sure they did not have any such weapons. I could stake my life on it"?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: What you say was returned was illegal. The police had distributed these weapons to the reserve forces. The Muslims were still in the reserve forces when Malko, after the attack on Renovica, ordered all long-barrelled weapons to be returned. They were all returned and that included these weapons that were distributed to the police. The standard Muslim police force in Pale had been disbanded, and the two men whose rifles and uniforms I said I returned, well, yes, I did do that. They couldn't take them with them. They asked me whether I could return them. I said I could and I returned them. I went to the police. The legal weapons were most probably returned. There was nothing illegal that was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct then, sir, that the Muslim inhabitants, the males of Pale municipality, retained the weapons that had been issued to them by the JNA in 1991 and all this entire period up until now that we are talking about, including up to the attack on Renovica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me better understand. Earlier I heard about police -- reserve police. In your question now it is JNA. Is that -- how do I have to?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours. I had stopped reading from the quotation before we went to the end. The witness has talked about the police and perhaps if I can -- let me -- let me first ask him about the police and then we can finish the quotation and then ask him about the others and it will become clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, am I correct that the Muslim habitants, the males of Pale municipality, retained the weapons that had been issued to them by the police in 1991 and all the way up this entire period up until now, including up until after the attack on Renovica?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I don't have any precise information as to when the reserve policemen were mobilised. I don't have any precise information. But I did see them when they went on patrol. They were wearing those winter police uniforms, not the summer ones, and they had semi-automatic rifles on them. I saw that myself. They didn't have to return these weapons to the police because every day they were involved in carrying out checks of some kind. When they were ordered to return the weapons, they returned them. But as to when these weapons were issued, I don't know. I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now if we could return to the segment from the Karadzic trial, and we left off at line 13. I'd like to read from line 14 onwards and have you comment on that, sir. So again I will quote so you can get the translation of what was said during that trial, starting with line 14: "Q. That was in keeping with the Tito's doctrine of armed population? "A. Yes. I don't think how long they kept -- they got to keep the uniforms and the equipment, I mean registered reserve policemen. These were not distributed to other regular people. And when this announcement came, some of these reserve policemen did not have the courage to bring it in themselves to the police station. "Q. I agree about the reserve policemen, but were you ever called up to do an exercise as a military reservist? "A. Yes. "Q. At that time would you also take the uniform and sometimes the weapon home? "A. First of all, I could not drive an armoured vehicle back to my home. "Q. Yes, but infantrymen could take weapons home, couldn't they? "A. Yes." End of quotation. And we're now on page 1211 of that transcript. Sir, do you recall this testimony from the Karadzic trial that you participated in in, I believe, 2010.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd just like to clarify the record regarding the previous line of questioning. Initially, Mr. Ivetic had identified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may do so. You are not supposed to comment at this moment, although I might have comment on some of the questions, but you can do that in re-examination. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise, Your Honour. You said you had a comment on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I wait for your next question and I might comment then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to this part of the Karadzic transcript and your testimony, would you agree with me that it was possible for Muslim males and also males of other ethnicities who had been called up for exercises in Pale municipality to have been issued equipment, including weapons and uniforms, and kept them this entire period, including up until after the attack on Renovica village that we have discussed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said just a minute ago --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, respectfully, the document that Mr. Ivetic used to start this line of questioning is dated April 1992. He has dated the attack in May 1992, and so I'm not sure why he thinks this line of questioning is relevant to the attack on Renovica village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's, again, comment. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To respond or?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, can I get an answer to my question. For your sake let me repeat it, sir. With respect to this part of the Karadzic transcript and your testimony, would you agree with me that it was possible for Muslim males and also males of other ethnicities who had been called up for exercises in Pale municipality to have been issued equipment, including weapons and uniforms, and to have kept them this entire period including up until after the attack on Renovica village that we have discussed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, just to clarify, Mr. Ivetic is not asking whether they took any weapons home but whether that was possible. Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will. It wasn't possible because at that time, at the time of the crisis, the Muslims did not receive any call-up papers. No one tried to mobilise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were there scheduled exercises in 1990, 1991?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Not the usual military exercises. No such exercises had been planned, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then where did these reserve policemen whose rifles you returned, where did they get their weapons if they had not been mobilised and had not been called for exercises?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Well, I have answered that question. And now you're asking me about military weapons or whether the army distributed weapons. I answered your question with regard to the police. The police mobilised them and they were given weapons, the reservists were. But as for the army, there was no attempt to mobilise the -- the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I'll now come with my comment. You start a line of questioning, asking the witness that the Bosnian Muslim population there had access not only to hunting and sport guns but also to automatic rifles. A few lines further down, you said: "Would you agree with me that the Muslim males in Praca possessed not only hunting and sport guns but also had access to automatic rifles." And then you create an inconsistency with some people perhaps having kept, due to the police service, having kept. That is misleading. That is creating an inconsistency which doesn't exist yet. If you had asked in the beginning: Are you aware whether any man had any such weapon and what happened to those weapons, then you most likely would have received the answers as the witness gives them now. It takes an awful lot of time, you're confusing the witness, and it's the third time today that the Chamber has to correct you on creating non-existing contradictions. Please keep this in mind when you continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I must take exception because you are not looking at page 57, line 2, where I asked specifically did proceed by asking about the Bosnian Muslim population in Pale municipality generally and asked him whether he agreed with the proposition. He then said he wouldn't and then he started answering about Renovica, and then I went specifically to Praca because the testamentary relates to Praca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where did you limit -- in paragraph 57? I put to you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On page 57.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Page 57, line?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're asking about Praca. Line 2: "I put it to you, sir, that in Pale municipality, specifically in Praca..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Bosnian Muslim population, that is a broad characteristic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In Praca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it your suggestion that all the Bosnian Muslim population in Praca had access to or that individuals in Praca may have had such weapons? That's not the same, Mr. Ivetic. I take it that you're aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm aware it's not the same. It's -- we're -- okay. I stand corrected on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct, sir, that the SDA leadership in Sarajevo explicitly told Muslims of Pale and the rest of Bosnia not to respond to mobilisation call-ups?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: No one gave us that information. The then-authorities in the municipality of Pale simply didn't send call-up papers to us, and we had no contact with Sarajevo whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the SDA leadership in Sarajevo telling Bosnian Muslims not to respond to the mobilisation call-ups -- or, pardon me. Let's make it very simple: Are you aware of the SDA leadership in Sarajevo explicitly telling everyone not to respond to the mobilisation call-up?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I am unaware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can I offer to refresh your recollection by the fact that in two trials before this Tribunal you have testified that you were aware of that, including the Zupljanin transcript, the 21st of June, 2010, transcript page 11997, lines 10 through 15, and the Krajisnik transcript, 2 September 2004, transcript page 5365 through 5366. Do I need to pull them up, sir?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: If you bear with me, I'll tell you. This is what I know. Alija Izetbegovic suggested that the young men that were supposed to serve their military term should not go. I don't know anything about the entire -- the overall population.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's see if we can move forward. Do you recall that immediately before your arrest, there was an incident in Sarajevo where Bosnian Muslim individuals had attacked a Serb wedding in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes. That is how the media reported. In Stari Grad, a Serb person was killed at a wedding, and everyone seemed to believe that. However, when I was in Sarajevo inquiring about it, they said that there were demonstrations taking place and that the person who was killed -- I don't know if I can speak freely? That they were provoking.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm not interested in the incident as I am in the time-period. Keeping in mind when that time -- when that incident occurred, sir, and perhaps -- well, let me do it the easy way. Let me call up your testimony from the Krajisnik trial. T -- 1D284, page 5 in e-court. It starts at line 11. Here it goes -- again, sir, I will read so you get the translation: "Q. I think what I asked you was whether you recall that. Are you saying that at the time you didn't know anything about such matters? "A. There were check-points towards Sarajevo and towards Pale, but I myself didn't see what those people at the check-points in Sarajevo did. I didn't go there so I can't say. "Q. Were you aware that they were what might be rather crudely referred to as 'Muslim check-points'? "A. Yes they were." Now, first, sir, I want to ask you, do you recall this testimony that you gave in Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I do recall it well. When I was asked about that instance, I wasn't able to recall things, and they asked me several times. Each time I said I didn't know. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First, before we get to that, are these check-points that you are talking about in Krajisnik check-points that arose immediately after this incident in Sarajevo where this wedding was attacked?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I can't say anything precisely about the check-points. I do know that at one check-point people stopped coming through to work from Sarajevo to Pale. That's the only check-point I can refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to Pale itself, am I correct that as of May 1992 there were many refugees coming to Pale from not only surrounding villages but also from Sarajevo, such that there are about 15.000 refugees and the food supplies were said to be getting low?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's a compound question. Perhaps if Mr. Ivetic could break it up so the witness can answer it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct, sir, that with respect to Pale itself, as of May 1992, there were many refugees coming to Pale not only from the surrounding villages but also from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes, they started coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You were asked about -- well, strike that. Would you agree with me that there were estimates that approximately 15.000 refugees, as of May 1992, had come to Pale?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I would agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you also agree that the food supplies in Pale were said to be getting low because of this excess number of people that were in Pale?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I know that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you also agree with me that the tensions in Pale, or the rise in tensions in Pale, according to you, were in part -- were in part arising from this large wave of refugees? If you understand the question. If not, I will rephrase it by going to something you testified about earlier.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes, of course we were afraid. People were coming. People we didn't know. And they would say, I came from the front lines, I came from combat, and he had hand-grenades around his belt, knives, weapons. Of course we were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that during this period another factor which you identify as contributing to the rise of tensions in Pale was an attack performed by Muslims against Serbs in Zepa on the 4th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Muslims did not attack Serbs in Zepa. There were basically no Serbs in Zepa. There was a column going from Sokolac to Zepa, and I guess the people there defended themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You were asked about this in the Krajisnik trial, and am I correct, sir, that you agreed, although you didn't know the actual number, that a great number of Serb young men from Pale were killed in this attack on a -- on a column passing by Zepa?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Transcript page, please, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. The transcript page would be 5391 through 5392 in Krajisnik. It is 1D284, pages 8 through 9 in e-court, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Starting at line -- line 10, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, now, sir, I apologise. Let me restate my question. Am I correct, sir, that although you don't know the actual number, that a great number of Serb young men from Pale were killed on this attack on a column passing by Zepa.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I was in no position to learn about the numerical strength of either those who were killed or the other side. I could -- I only knew that there were helicopters used to communicate with Zepa, and -- but I didn't know anything about numbers, and they used the helicopters for the food and the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps if I can direct your attention and let me read this for you, sir, to be fair. This is line 13 of what is on the screen through line 17. And again, it's a quotation from the Krajisnik trial: "Q. And about 45 or about 45 soldiers were killed by Muslims in that attack, weren't they? "A. I don't know the number. I don't know how many people were killed, those young men who were Serbs from Pale. But I do know that the number was quite high." Sir, does that refresh your recollection and am I correct that -- that this is what you testified to -- in the -- in the Krajisnik case.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes, I testified to that. And I repeated that I know there were quite a few who were killed, but I don't know any specific figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And during this time-period when tensions were high in Pale, at paragraph 31 of your statement, you talk about certain paramilitary criminals who you identify as not being in the army who were going around and harassing people. I'd like to ask you, if you recall, that during this time-period, the authorities in Pale, that is, the police authorities and the army, undertook to disarm and arrest a group of paramilitary criminals that had been in the Mali Dom who had been harassing both Serbs and Muslims in Pale?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: The traditional kind of mistreatment in private homes and apartments was not present, but we were afraid the moment such an armed person would show up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have knowledge of the police and army authorities in Pale arresting a group of criminals who had been -- operating near the Mali Dom in Pale who had been harassing Serbs and Muslims in Pale during this period when tensions were high?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: This name, Mali Dom, is not familiar to me. There is a so-called Turisticki Dom that I know but that's far from me, the other end of Pale. I couldn't possibly know what was going on there. And I don't know why you call these men criminals. I know exactly what a criminal is. This thing that was happening in Pale was something entirely different. No question of criminals.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have knowledge or not of a large group of individuals that were arrested and disarmed by the authorities of Pale during this time-period for harassing Muslims and Serbs in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first try to split it up. Are you aware of people being arrested at that time apparently on suspicion of having arrest Serbs and Muslims? Do you know whether people were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the situation with Agan Kadaric [phoen] and his wife whose jewellery had been stolen by a certain of these persons you identify as paramilitaries, and that the police were able to get this jewellery back and returned it to Ms. Kadaric?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I know about that. And, yes, it happened the way you say. The jewellery was stolen but the police found out somehow, caught those people, and the jewellery was returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could just briefly look at 1D283. This is a proofing note. And I believe the -- the bottom paragraph, the last paragraph on the page, talks about this incident. And also talks -- says here, sir, and I'm reading from the bottom of the proofing note: "On another occasion, one person was removed from his flat. He complained and was allowed to return." Sir, is this another incident where these persons you identify as paramilitaries harassed individuals and the authorities -- the police authorities apprehended these paramilitaries and returned the rightful owner to his flat in Pale?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first ask the witness whether he has any knowledge about the incident before we ask him to comment on documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a proofing note of the interview with the Office of the Prosecutor and this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. Let me see. Yes, I missed that. Apologies for that. Could you answer the question, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I know that person. His name is Nasko Smajic. He was arrested, and I'm not sure if he spent the night in custody, and then he was released. But then the police caught up with him and somebody set him up, put a rifle that we called the Gypsy, and he was found with it, and he was taken in again, and he never came out of the police station alive again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. We have your testimony. I'd like to now move to discuss the exchange of residence that you undertook and which is discussed at page 61 through 63 of your statement, which is Exhibit P260.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For e-court, it's page 11 in English and pages 20 to 21 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And herein you describe the transfer of your house to an individual named Ms. Dragica Subotic. First of all, with respect to paragraph 61 of your statement, I put it to you that paragraph 61 is not entirely accurate because this paragraph does not identify that you actually co-owned your home with your brother, Taib. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: No, you're not correct. We were owners of the building 2/1. It was in the land register and it also verified by a court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say "we." Did you mean you and your brother or?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. My brother and I. I mean to say that the two of us were owners of that house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you were both living in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both. We shared it. We lived in one part of the house, each.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can call up 65 ter number 03727, and I apologise, Your Honours, by my notes this was not tendered as an associated exhibit, although it is I believe referenced in the -- in the statement. So I apologise if there's a P number that I have somehow missed. But by my notes, it was not tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So while we wait for 65 ter 03727, sir, can you look on the screen. Does this appear to be the contract that you signed, along with your brother and Ms. Subotic, in relation to your home?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down to the signatures. Does that appear to have the signatures of all persons concerned?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Yes, they're there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to part IV of this contract, wherein it states: "The contracting parties hereby undertake that the use and looking after ... the property under contract shall be temporary and shall last until the war eases and the conditions for normal life are achieved, at which time the final status of the property under contract shall be resolved by agreement with the mandatory consent of the contracting parties." Sir, this contract does not, in fact, transfer ownership but envisions the right to use of property that shall be temporary until the war conditions are over; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Look at the date on this document. On the same day, after 2.00 p.m., I found myself on the way to Sarajevo on a bus. I had no time to think anything over. I was going straight from there to the bus. And this was a very important document. It was important to Dragica Subotic, so that she can take -- get into the house. It didn't matter to me. There you are, here I am. I want to swap something with you, and you are taking in exchange something you have never seen and you have to agree to it. I had no opportunity to see that property, and, of course, I wasn't leaving my house of my own will. I had to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We'll get to all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would tender this document as the next available D exhibit before moving onto the next Prosecution document that I'd like to show this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 03727 shall be assigned Exhibit D54. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. ... I'm trying to understand why we have to establish that this is not transfer of ownership.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Because the witness's statement in paragraphs 61 through 63. First of all, the heading says "Forcible Transfer of Muslim Property."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in paragraphs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it true that property is transferred not ownership by property?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The contracting parties shall take possession of the property under contract. That is, therefore, a transfer of property. And it says nowhere in 61 or 62, it's not even suggested, that ownership is transferred. Even the witness is quite clear on that. Some kind of a contract. So apart, of course, what is the core of the testimony of the witness, that he was not free to -- not to sign, that he was under such circumstances that he was -- he couldn't do anything else. Now you are focussing on what seems to be an issue which is relatively marginal in this whole matter, because it's not about the formal aspect of ownership. And apart from that, you are telling me that this is about ownership and you're correcting something which is not contained in the statement. Or do I misread the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I read the statement and again I'm perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then tell me where the transfer of ownership is mentioned in paragraph 61 and 62.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 62. 62. "I did not give up my house voluntarily. They were not voluntarily surrendering their property and none of us voluntarily surrendered our property." And again, I am coloured by the fact that I have the witness's testimony in three other trials where the insinuation was made that this was a transfer of ownership.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll check that, then. But at least to the extent you told me that this is what the document says, you would agree with me that the document is talking about the transfer of property and that is the language the witness used at least in his statement, and that no mention is made in any way of ownership. But if there are other matters, then you should have taken the witness to those parts of the testimony where ownership is dealt with. Here it is not. At least -- unless you tell me where to find it. And we all know that property and ownership is not the same, isn't is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you consider this as a contract whereby you were being forced to give up ownership of your property?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: You're asking me now to comment on legal aspects. I'm only saying that I was forced to sign that contract. Now about ownership and property and things likes that, are not something I can speak about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. With regard to paragraph 61 of your statement, you discuss the negotiations with Ms. Subotic to transfer your house temporarily to her. I'd like to ask you: Is it correct that you undertook these negotiations with Ms. Subotic or was it, in fact, your brother who undertook all of these discussions with Ms. Subotic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: My brother talked to Dragica Subotic, and I honoured my brother, even though he is dead now, and I did not contradict him. But if it had been up to me, I don't know how it would have ended. It may be that I would not have survived the war but I would surely not leave my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that your late brother basically ran this whole business about the exchange and that you had very little to do with it, apart from signing your name on the document?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: None of us had any time. It all happened on the same day when we had to leave the house. We didn't have time to discuss anything and what to do and what is best. We could see what was going on around us and we thought we needed to save our heads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, were you present when your brother spoke, your late brother, spoke to -- to Dragica Subotic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not the first part of their discussions, I wasn't present. I joined them when they had already almost agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if you still remember, at what time in the day you left from Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At what time - to the extent you remember - did Dragica Subotic come to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She didn't actually come to see me at all. My late wife told me, There's a woman calling on your brother. It could have been 11.00 a.m. when I found out about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you or your brother have known her before she then came to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we didn't know her. Nobody knew her before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, once you signed, you would be aware of the existence of Dragica Subotic for two hours, approximately, or a little bit over two hours? Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not earlier than that. I had known her for about two or three hours before I left my house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You say you had known her for two or three hours. Is it correct that your brother met with her the day before and discussed the transfer -- temporary transfer of the property?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, do you positively know that she did not come the day before or are you not aware that she may have come the day before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose my brother would have told me for sure if he had -- if she had come the day before. I can't say that she had visited earlier than I saw her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic. I'm looking also looking at the clock, Mr. Ivetic. How much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I need at least five to seven minutes to finish up with this line of questioning, which was to be my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And after that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which was to be my last. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I suggest that you finish in the next seven minutes and that we take the break slightly later than we usually do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And this Subotic family, am I correct that this lady and her son did not prevent you from taking anything from the home that you wished?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: They did not. But what was I supposed to carry? On my back or where? I could take only what I could carry in my two hands onto the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct, sir, that you did, in fact, get possession of your home back in 2002 and everything there was still intact and preserved?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I got the house back, but I didn't find anything inside. No furniture. And there are still traces of the axe that was used to get the floorboards off. And all the shelves and everything we had from -- from floor to ceiling, that was all gone. I -- I did get the house back, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall meeting the son, Mr. Miro Subotic, who was present during the signing of the contract that his mother signed?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: His mother introduced him. We only met at the municipality, in the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can call up 1D292. This is a statement given by Miro Subotic to the Karadzic Defence team that was disclosed to us by the Office of the Prosecutor on the EDS system, and I would like to ask for the witness's comment on some items on page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, do you intend to tender this or to -- otherwise you could read from it because it might be not in line with Rule 92 bis or ter to use it in evidence, so if you want read a portion of it and then have it marked for identification that would be the most appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was even just going to read it but have it up on the screen so people could follow, so that the court reporters and translators can have an easier time keeping up with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Obviously I'm only interested in what the witness knows or does not know about these items. This is on page 3 at the top in the B/C/S and the bottom of page 2 in the English. And the paragraph I would like to start with is the third from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, I will read for you since I do see that this -- that the B/C/S version is in Cyrillic and I do not know whether you can read Cyrillic: "The brothers, Taib and Sulejman, together with a large group of their countrymen, left Pale in an organised fashion in a bus convoy, probably on the same day. They all left voluntarily, based on their own requests [sic] and without any kind of harassment. "I personally helped Taib and Sulejman carry their things to the bus. We parted on friendly terms, and Sulejman's allegations which I have become acquainted with, that someone threatened them and forced them out of their house, are not true." First of all, sir, is it correct that Mr. Subotic and the Subotic family assisted you and your brother in carrying things to the bus?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Miro is not fair and he is not sincere. He didn't help me and I don't think he helped my brother. They did come to check whether we were, indeed, going to board the buses for Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'm now going to ask you about the entirety of these two paragraphs that I read to you from this statement of Mr. Subotic. Do you -- do you agree that they accurately reflect the situation or not? That is, do you agree with it or do you take issue with it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With what, exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: These two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's a lot in these two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, the entirety. Do they accurately reflect the events that transpired or not, whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, you've asked many questions -- many questions were asked about the subjects covered by these where the witness clearly said he did not agree. So therefore to ask him now to agree on the whole of it seems to be not --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking -- I'm asking whether he takes issue with the entirety of it, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The two paragraphs, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The third from the bottom and the second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, the one starting with --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "The brothers Taib and Sulejman ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think you already testified that you -- that you were not helped by Miro carrying their things to the bus, isn't it? Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you -- did you part on friendly terms with this family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not. They did watch us board the buses, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you agree that you were not threatened and forced to leave the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't drive us out, but they did hurry us along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean they, the mother and the son did not drive you out. But I did understand your testimony to be that -- that you were forced not by these persons but you were forced out of the -- of Pale.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. I was forced by the Serbian Democratic Party and by Koljevic himself who stated, Serbs won't live with the Muslims together in Pale. What else is necessary?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have one more question for you. You -- you got the house back, you said, a few years after the war. I think you said 2002. Do you remember -- how did you get it back? Was it voluntarily transferred to you, or did you have to go to court for it or?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, when I submitted an application to recover my house, there was some international non-governmental organisation at work, they were involved, and I went through them. They went to the municipality to get some documents to check that we were indeed the owners, Sulejman and Taib, and based on those documents they realised we were indeed the owners, and then they started proceedings to recover the house for us. But there was this international CRPC organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was not that Mrs. Subotic voluntarily left the house and returned it to you, you had to go to court. Do I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't go to court myself. It is very likely that the CRPC people did. Dragica, may she rest in peace, died before I succeeded in getting the house back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But she remained living in the house when you had started the -- or when the court proceedings had started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. She died before the procedure of return was set in motion. Two of her sons, Miro and Zoran, were in the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They continued to live there when proceedings were started. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We are beyond the time where we usually take the break. Mr. Ivetic, how much time would you still -- how many questions would you still have, I would say, because I think after six out of the seven minutes you said you would needed I intervened which would leave you one minute. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have five questions, Your Honours, including one citation from this -- from this statement of Mr. Subotic that goes into some of the matters that Your Honour has raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we first have to take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But could the witness first leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at ten minutes to 2.00. And for the five questions, you have five minutes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed. You've got five minutes for your last questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, the Subotic family, just to be clear, they were Serb refugees who had been expelled from their home in the Pofalici neighbourhood of Sarajevo by armed Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I don't know what had happened to them. I just know they showed up at Pale. I don't know how they left the city. I can't comment on that, and they didn't mention it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to return to the statement by Mr. Miro Subotic, and I'd like to skip to the next page in English, whereas on the B/C/S it's still on the same page just skipping one paragraph, and I read the paragraph that begins at the top. So it's page 3 in the English: "I left the house owned by the Crncalo brothers in the presence of representatives of the Commissariat for Refugees and Displaced Persons of the municipality of Pale. On that occasion a report was drafted which clearly shows that the house was returned in good condition. My brother and I even added a fence on the balcony which was not there before and did that at our own expense. That is when I gave the representatives of the Commissariat the house key, which was reported in the inventory. Hence, my family and I, my brother's family, and my late mother abided by all six provisions in the contract on exchange signed by us and the brothers Taib and Sulejman Crncalo." Is it correct that you received a report from the Commissariat for Refugees and Displaced Persons and an inventory relating to the condition of the property when it was returned to you in 2003, I believe?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I was prohibited from being present when the key was handed over. The report was drafted by a person from the Commissariat and it was drafted only once I arrived at the house with that person. Miro never even jokingly mentioned my car, let alone returned it. It was a Fiat 125P and it had only 33 kilometres on the clock. It was almost new --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 33.000 kilometres on the clock.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, he didn't even need to return it. I'm just happy to be alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can now turn to the convoy after this. Am I correct, sir -- or strike that. I have information that the convoy was arranged by a Bosnian Muslim SDA official with the authorities and that the individual's name is Mr. Ahmed Palo who is the vice-president of the Pale municipality before the war. Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Ahmed's last name is Palo. On paper, he was deputy head of municipality, but as for his ability to organise such a convoy, well, he lived some 20-plus kilometres away from the Pale municipality towards the east. He had no access to the centre of Pale so as to able to organise any convoys. It was organised by the SDS. No one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I understand your testimony. We will check up on that. Now, with respect to the convoy that was under the police escort, as I believe you had identified in your statement, am I correct that the entire convoy was able to travel over to the demarcation line between the warring factions and that everyone arrived in Sarajevo without suffering any harassment or any injuries. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: That is correct. No one touched us. We arrived at a location at Zeca Glava, and then we had to go down to the city on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I thank you for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have any further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any need for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Crncalo, Mr. Ivetic just read you at temporary transcript page 85 a portion of Miro Subotic's statement discussing the condition of the properties you had exchanged. Can you describe for the Chamber the condition of the property in Sarajevo which the Subotics had left when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I can. I was provided an address, a street and house number. Once I arrived there with my bags, I wanted to get in, but more than half of the house was gone. It was destroyed by a shell. If it had been in good condition -- a fortnight later, another two shells landed and it wouldn't have amounted to much anyhow. Had I been in the house at that moment, I would have died too. In any case, once I approached the house for the first time, I realised that half of it was gone, blown up by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And were you able to stay there?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I couldn't. There was no way. There was nowhere to stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Next, sir, Mr. Ivetic inquired with you about conflict in Pale municipality. Were the people in your convoy who you stated were forced to leave Pale, were they fighting then?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: There were people like myself with wives and children, with their luggage. It wasn't much to look at. One couldn't even think they were fighters. If they were fighters, they would have been arrested, taken away to the police or elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And finally, sir, when you found yourself in the Sarajevo morgue on 28 August 1995, you said you saw several people there who had passed away. Were any of those people wearing military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: They were all women. There was seven bodies of women lying next to each other. What sort of uniform? There were no uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that concludes my re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, is my recollection right that state in which the witness found the house in Sarajevo already appears in the statement, that it was hit by a shell and that it --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's briefly discussed in paragraph 61, Your Honour, in P260.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apparently you didn't elicit any further evidence on the matter, so therefore I wonder whether it was needed at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has no further questions. Mr. Ivetic, have the questions in re-examination triggered any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They have not, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Crncalo, this concludes your evidence in this court. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, both by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you for allowing me to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the first thing I'd like to do is decide on the admission of D54, that is the -- that is admitted into evidence because there were no objections from the Defence. Anything other matter you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Two brief matters regarding exhibits. First, regarding Exhibit P260, Mr. Crncalo's statement, Mr. Ivetic cross-examined the witness at length about some of the redacted paragraphs from the statement, specifically paragraphs 13 and 14. We would seek leave to replace Exhibit P260 with an unredacted version as a result.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Totally unredacted or to remove the redactions of those paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Those two paragraphs, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that's paragraphs 13 and 13 are then -- what did you say to? No, 13 and 14 are -- Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour. And you'll see that that's where my questions came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then leave is granted that the -- that P260, the witness's statement, is replaced by a new version in which the paragraphs 13 and 14 are not further redacted. Are not redacted, I should say. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: There was one more matter regarding exhibits, Your Honour. Regarding Mr. Seselj's speech on 6 May 1991 which the Chamber inquired about and which was the subject of many of Mr. Ivetic's questions, we have located the video and transcripts on our exhibit list, 65 ter 22719A. And I'd invite Mr. Ivetic and the Defence to review those with a view to agreeing on admission of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When do we hear from you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could perhaps have the weekend we can take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. After the weekend we hear from you. If you agree, then of course the Chamber leaves it in your hands who will tender that. If not, the Chamber will consider whether it will instruct one of the parties to call it. But we'll first then think about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: With those brief matters having been addressed, Your Honour, I just seek to be excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you are excused. Mr. Groome, I know that you -- Yes, Mr. Lukic. Now -- I know -- let me first address you, Mr. Groome. I know that you do not have the half-hour which you intended to take. Is there any way of briefing the Chamber already in limited time and then perhaps summarise what you wanted to say and then have the remainder be submitted in writing or is there any -- I'm trying to find a practical solution for --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have actually a practical solution for the use of the remaining time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There was another report that the Chamber requested for today, and that was -- you requested it last Friday at transcript page 2858, and if you recall that has to do with the videotape, and you had asked Mr. Ivetic -- or you gave the Defence until today to report on their position. We did provide the Defence with our preliminary analysis as we had said that we would, and I've asked Ms. Bibles to come into the Chamber so we are prepared to deal with that, and I think that matter probably will fit within the time available remaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that is the case, are you -- any suggestion that you would submit in writing what you wanted to say about the other matter for which you needed half an hour? The Chamber noticed that often you have prepared your submissions often in writing. Is there any way that we could speed up without losing time with witnesses on that matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do do that to try to make sure that I say it as briefly as possible. Given everything that I'm trying accomplish these day, I'd appreciate just the opportunity to make -- to have this discussion with the Chamber and to not engage in a lengthy submission and counter-submission process. I think this is just some very -- very practical matters of guidance I'm seeking from the Chamber, and I think once the Chamber hears it, it's a matter that can move forward very quickly after that. And perhaps, Your Honour, I can say in a sentence essentially what I'll be seeking is we are filing a bar table motion with respect to the intercepts, and if I can give the Chamber all of the references on Monday where you've authorised us to do that, we'll file that Monday, and I believe that will be 19 witnesses if the Chamber were to grant all of the relief we sought. I'm also filing on Monday a notice of witnesses we may not call and that will be about 30 witnesses. So one of the things I am seeking the Chamber's guidance on: If we can suspend 92 bis applications on those two groups of witnesses, approximately 50 witnesses, until such time a little further down in the process and prioritise our time on the -- the remaining. And with respect to the remaining, the pace that we're filing them is set by the Chamber's guidance. We are seeking the ability to file them as soon as we have them done, recognising that that's a lot to ask the Defence to respond to in 14 days, but we feel that once they're before the Chamber and before the Defence they can decide how best to use their resources, and we would not oppose any application under 127 for an amendment of the time-period for them to respond. And I guess that, in a nutshell, was my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome we leave it to that at this very moment then. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just two brief things, Your Honour. First, the Prosecution filed a motion for additional protective measures for the Witness 081 and since it's an urgent matter we don't object to this motion, so we don't have to go through the process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much for that because that was on my list as well. It was only yesterday, I think, that the Prosecution filed that motion for augmentation. And it's not the first time, Mr. Groome, that such motions are filed at a time which - as I have it on my list - doesn't give the Defence sufficient time to respond. So you're invited to avoid in the future to have such late notice. And yesterday you said, Mr. Lukic, you were saved by the bell --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The bell, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and I think Mr. Groome is saved by your bell at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so it's clear, that's a witness that we were trying to advance so that we make full use of the time. If you remember earlier today, it was only today that we decided that we would call that witness. We were simply trying to give everyone as much notice as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not dramatically blaming you for it, but of course the Chamber is always a bit concerned if it receives motions where proper time for a Defence response seems to -- not to be there. Thank you, nevertheless, Mr. Lukic, for your quick response. Next matter you would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I discussed during the break with Mr. Groome the issue of acceptance of the 65 ter document 28432. That's the -- the list with documents. And I think that I explained to Mr. Groome why -- what was my confusion, and he agreed to tender the same documents through the same list with the Witness 511. So for now we are safe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the comments are there, the chart is there --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and the underlying documents will be tendered at later stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. That's roughly it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber appreciates that the parties agreed on that. Ms. Bibles, about the video. We do not have much time, but perhaps you could give it a start.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. As you can see I have no prepared comments. We simply wanted to request whether the Defence was going to answer the question posed last week. I think it was about the -- basically about the reliability of the video D43 simply to determine whether we do need to proceed with the formal forensic analysis. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just think about D43, which was the?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can help, it was the excerpt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The one video, the excerpt from -- was that the -- the journey to Omarska arriving from the south rather than from the north, to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I believe at the -- at the end of that session we'd looked at another videotape that -- it appeared to be from the same angle, and I said I believe it looks to be the same angle. The videotape we used we downloaded from the source and did not alter, so it's what it is. But then after all this questioning, the witness then clarified and said that this all occurred after he heard the shooting. So it kind of made the whole thing moot because in answers to cross-examination he'd said that this was the time period when the shooting occurred but then he testified later that this was all after the shooting had concluded. So I leave it to Your Honours -- or to the Prosecution as to do with that -- with that exhibit. We presented it in good faith based upon the original of that video which -- that was given to the Prosecution in full. So the excerpt that we showed was the actual video as we received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to -- we had a video, we then had a video with and without sound, and we had a competing video with different sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the main concern was about the competing video with the different sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was -- was that D43?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That was D43 as I recall, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you had asked if the competing video that was shown in re-direct, whether it appeared to be the same camera angle, and I believe it does appear to be the same camera angle. That's all I can say. I can't go beyond that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it true that there was more that the Prosecution wanted to also to investigate whether the sound was tampered with?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That was the issue that we posited to the Court. If I'm understanding Defence counsel, he is suggesting that he downloaded the video D43, and I'm guessing it was from the web site that was featured prominently on the video itself, and I simply would ask if Defence is indicating that they are no longer positing that as a reliable -- at least audio track, with respect to that, and I think that would bring the issue to a halt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to D43, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will consider whether or not it accepts this as a solution to the matter raised and we will let you know. We then adjourn for the day, with apologies for the late adjournment, and we will resume - let me just check - Monday, is that the 1st of October, I think. Monday, the 1st of October, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 1st day of October, 2012, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.19 p.m.,
